extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism adjudication from XML/PDF results, Figure 10/11 captions, methods text, and linked DRAMP mechanism notes.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Vv-AMP1 treatment is directly associated with fungal membrane permeabilization in a propidium iodide uptake fluorescence microscopy assay.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Vv-AMP1-treated Fusarium oxysporum, Fusarium solani, and Verticillium dahliae hyphae

assay_conditions.incubation: 25 C for 40 h before PI staining
assay_conditions.stain: 25 μg/ml propidium iodide in PBS for 10 min

mechanism_claims.limitations: The paper phrases the mechanism cautiously; PI uptake supports membrane compromise but does not identify a receptor or molecular target.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=12:Antimicrobial activity of Vv-AMP1; xml:fig=10:Figure 10; xml:sec=31:Antimicrobial activity of recombinant Vv-AMP1

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Vv-AMP1 shows non-morphogenic antifungal activity by inhibiting hyphal elongation and producing swollen hyphal tips/granulated cytoplasm rather than hyperbranching.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: fungal hyphae in the antifungal assay panel
mechanism_claims.limitations: Microscopy observations are phenotypic and do not define a molecular target.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=12:Antimicrobial activity of Vv-AMP1; xml:sec=16:Inhibition profile and antifungal characteristics

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Vv-AMP1 retained antifungal activity after heat treatment but lost activity after proteinase K digestion, supporting heat stability and proteinaceous activity.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: recombinant Vv-AMP1 stability assays against Botrytis cinerea and Verticillium dahliae
mechanism_claims.limitations: Stability assays characterize peptide robustness, not a direct antimicrobial mode of action.
